fields.Core Themes JSON: [{"title": "The Mountain That Might Be a Pachyderm", "body": "The centerpiece of the conversation is Spain's Montgo massif, which Stellium7 argues may be the petrified remains of a colossal pachyderm rather than ordinary rock. He notes the formation reads as an elephant lying on its side from multiple angles, that a local restaurant once used it as a logo, and that a cave sits precisely where an eye socket belongs. He says he hiked it for eight years without the thought ever occurring to him, then found roughly ten anatomical features in a single hour on Google Earth once he entertained the possibility."}, {"title": "Biology Underneath the Geology Textbook", "body": "Stellium7 contends that even the mainstream account concedes most rock was once alive, with igneous stone the exception, and that sedimentary and metamorphic layers are compressed plant and animal remains. His departure is timescale: he argues petrification can happen fast rather than across hundreds of millions of years. He points to Lake Natron, whose alkaline water hardens creatures that fall in, to Mother Shipton's Cave in the UK where hung objects turn stony within months, and to Mount St. Helens, where he says layering and micro layering formed in a matter of hours."}, {"title": "Gravity, Pressure and the Case for Giants", "body": "The textbook objection to titanic creatures is weight: double a sphere's diameter and volume grows eightfold, so giants would break their own bones. Stellium7 counters that the objection depends entirely on gravity being what we are told, and he favors density, buoyancy and electrostatics as the operative forces. He notes the mainstream itself grants gigantism, citing meter long dragonflies, and asks how big the bears and elephants were. Chance adds that air may simply be a lighter density of water, and Stellium7 describes a pressurized room producing tens of thousands of oversized cherry tomatoes."}, {"title": "Titanic Trees and the Fractal Realm", "body": "Stellium7 says it was the tree question that pulled him in, seeded by the video No Forests on Flat Earth and its claim that plateaus like Devil's Tower are stumps. He treats the stumps as only one data point and considers better evidence elsewhere, citing a tour of the South Dakota Badlands with the Hangman 1128 channel and trees he describes as miles wide at the base. He notes lava tubes resembling root structures, and both men trace the branching Lichtenberg or dendritic pattern through lightning, rivers, blood vessels and the fascial network."}, {"title": "Pareidolia, Debunkers and the Ultracrepidarian", "body": "Stellium7 says he knew about pareidolia and apophenia before he ever looked at the mountain, and dismisses most creature shaped rock formations as exactly that. To guard against it he drew up a list of features he expected in an eye socket beforehand, consulted anatomy books, video of an elephant skeleton and 3D rendering software, noting seven bones form the orbit across mammals. He says critics invoked Dunning Kruger without reviewing his work, prompting a three hour rebuttal that took six weeks. Chance offers the word ultracrepidarian, and argues pareidolia is a perceptual superpower rather than a defect."}]
fields.Intro Paragraph 1: Mike Wilkerson of Stellium7 on Youtube joins InnerVerse to discuss his research on Bio-Geology and the ways in which organic material becomes petrified. Is the earth below our feet made from the remains of ancient mega-fauna? What does the mainstream say about the possibility that aside from igneous stone, all rock was once alive? We discuss all of this and more, including theories about the shrinking of life forms over eons, ubiquitous fractal patterns, & sonoluminescence.
fields.Intro Paragraph 2: In the Plus+ Extension we talk about the infamous Montgo titanic elephant, more fascinating petrification possibilities, histology of geological materials, biological transmutations unrecognized by "the science," unanswered questions about Mike's Titan, the evidence for super-massive petrified trees, heart-stones, research synchronicities, and the panpsychism of stone.

fields.Plus Core Themes JSON: [{"title": "A Mountain of Coincidences, Weighed as Odds", "body": "Chance opens the extension with the list of more than fifty coincidences, and Mike explains why the specific ones matter most to him. With the head tilted the way the mountain's is, he says an elephant's infraorbital foramen would sit in front of the eye socket, and a long cave runs perpendicular to the eye cave in just that spot. Inside, two overlapping stone surfaces trace the line where the frontal bone and maxilla would meet. He later predicted an ear, found a crescent of red rock at 375 meters, and learned a cave archaeologists had excavated and scanned in 3D sits in its center."}, {"title": "Reading the Mountain's Tissue", "body": "Moving from anatomy to histology, Mike says four materials turn up all over the massif: red earth, iron ore, quartz crystal and limestone, which he likens to bone, blood and plasma. The Swiss cheese limestone, with channels that branch into smaller perpendicular channels, reminds him of trabecular bone more than water erosion. Dried blood plasma forms flakes that look like quartz, so he theorizes that fatty tissues petrify into quartz. When a geologist mocked him, he took a thousand power microscope to the rock, found no shell or coral, and concluded that limestone is simply calcium carbonate, which in his view means bone."}, {"title": "Petrification Without the Millions of Years", "body": "Mike argues the permineralization timeline falls apart, citing wood that petrifies within seven years in mineral rich volcanic water and lab work that does it in twenty four hours. Chance compares geological dating to dark matter, a fudge that protects the theory. Mike then separates plasma transmutation, shown by a YouTuber fusing two powders into ruby inside a microwave, from biological transmutation, citing Louis Kervran, the hen whose diet cannot account for her eggshells, and a potted tree that gained mass on distilled water and sunlight. His conclusion is that biology makes the elements, and then it can turn to stone."}, {"title": "The Body as the Alchemical Laboratory", "body": "Chance takes the transmutation thread inward, recalling the alchemists' teaching that the body is the real laboratory and wondering whether a coherent enough person could transmute whatever they need rather than lean on supplements. He describes biofield tuning clients whose trouble with a certain food eased after work on the sacral center, with no probiotics or cleanse. Later he asks whether the rocks ever talk back, mentions his own experiences with crystals, and points to the dwarves in The Rings of Power who sing to the stone. For him, wonder and awe are the purpose of life here."}, {"title": "Doubt, Heart Stones and Synchronicity", "body": "Mike admits he still has doubts, even after two friends he led into the eye cave put their confidence at 110 percent, and he declines to make claims about nearby elephant shaped peaks that have no caves. The heart stones began with one river rock showing fifteen, then twenty three anatomical features, and he now has hundreds, with spectroscopy as his hoped for next step. A documentary on Francisco Torrent Guasp, who unrolled the heart into one spiraling band, led him to notice suture lines and a twist in his stones, and the cardiologist turned out to have worked at the foot of Montgó."}]

fields.Plus Quotes JSON: [{"text": "So right off the bat, we know that petrified wood can be created artificially in the blink of an eye. And yet they're telling us 200 to 300 million years.", "author": "Mike Wilkerson", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/3eef32c0-d5ef-4deb-97db-8c86743e4b62/MIKE-WILKERSON.jpg?content-type=image%2Fjpeg"}, {"text": "In terms of geology and archeology, the dating systems that they use are akin to dark matter and dark energy in astrophysics.", "author": "Chance Garton", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/a784fd99-3e6f-436c-a8f3-c4f913b855ed/profile-pic.jpg?content-type=image%2Fjpeg"}, {"text": "I'm of the mind now that everything that we see in one way or another is coming from biology, and then it can petrify.", "author": "Mike Wilkerson", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/3eef32c0-d5ef-4deb-97db-8c86743e4b62/MIKE-WILKERSON.jpg?content-type=image%2Fjpeg"}, {"text": "The ancient alchemists have been telling us for a long time, whether covertly or outright, that your body is the real alchemical laboratory.", "author": "Chance Garton", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/a784fd99-3e6f-436c-a8f3-c4f913b855ed/profile-pic.jpg?content-type=image%2Fjpeg"}, {"text": "A lot of the people that have been following my channel, they have more confidence in my findings and potential conclusions than I do.", "author": "Mike Wilkerson", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/3eef32c0-d5ef-4deb-97db-8c86743e4b62/MIKE-WILKERSON.jpg?content-type=image%2Fjpeg"}, {"text": "Life in existence is the only thing that exists. So everything comes from life itself.", "author": "Chance Garton", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/a784fd99-3e6f-436c-a8f3-c4f913b855ed/profile-pic.jpg?content-type=image%2Fjpeg"}, {"text": "We'd all understand that when we're looking at the stones, we're seeing the ancestors.", "author": "Mike Wilkerson", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/3eef32c0-d5ef-4deb-97db-8c86743e4b62/MIKE-WILKERSON.jpg?content-type=image%2Fjpeg"}, {"text": "At the end of the day, I think wonder and awe is the purpose of our life here. It's not supposed to be like, here's your manual, here's what everything is and how it works.", "author": "Chance Garton", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/a784fd99-3e6f-436c-a8f3-c4f913b855ed/profile-pic.jpg?content-type=image%2Fjpeg"}, {"text": "Either the universe is just playing with me and just toying with me, or I'm being guided to having these insights and revelations.", "author": "Mike Wilkerson", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/3eef32c0-d5ef-4deb-97db-8c86743e4b62/MIKE-WILKERSON.jpg?content-type=image%2Fjpeg"}, {"text": "Do the stones speak to me? If they do, they speak to me through synchronicity.", "author": "Mike Wilkerson", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/3eef32c0-d5ef-4deb-97db-8c86743e4b62/MIKE-WILKERSON.jpg?content-type=image%2Fjpeg"}]
fields.Quotes JSON: [{"text": "Most notably that all matter is biological and that life, existence, and material are synonymous phenomena.", "author": "Chance Garton", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/a784fd99-3e6f-436c-a8f3-c4f913b855ed/profile-pic.jpg?content-type=image%2Fjpeg"}, {"text": "I just started to look at stones differently. I often would see rock formations and puzzle over how they could have come about.", "author": "Stellium7", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/3eef32c0-d5ef-4deb-97db-8c86743e4b62/MIKE-WILKERSON.jpg?content-type=image%2Fjpeg"}, {"text": "There's so many mainstream scientists that have actually debunked cornerstones of the geological narrative. But it never seems to unravel the whole narrative.", "author": "Stellium7", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/3eef32c0-d5ef-4deb-97db-8c86743e4b62/MIKE-WILKERSON.jpg?content-type=image%2Fjpeg"}, {"text": "And if you don't have gravity, as they tell us, then those reasons for why we couldn't have had gigantic trees and gigantic creatures, those reasons are thrown out.", "author": "Stellium7", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/3eef32c0-d5ef-4deb-97db-8c86743e4b62/MIKE-WILKERSON.jpg?content-type=image%2Fjpeg"}, {"text": "We're underwater right now. They're restoring movement in a joint that has aberrant movement and creating sonoluminescence.", "author": "Stellium7", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/3eef32c0-d5ef-4deb-97db-8c86743e4b62/MIKE-WILKERSON.jpg?content-type=image%2Fjpeg"}, {"text": "I'd been hiking it for eight years and I never once thought this used to be a creature.", "author": "Stellium7", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/3eef32c0-d5ef-4deb-97db-8c86743e4b62/MIKE-WILKERSON.jpg?content-type=image%2Fjpeg"}, {"text": "But I have more of an opinion that pareidolia is a superpower rather than a perceptual problem.", "author": "Chance Garton", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/a784fd99-3e6f-436c-a8f3-c4f913b855ed/profile-pic.jpg?content-type=image%2Fjpeg"}]
